title: Planet Crisis Response — Bhote Koshi–Trishuli Outburst Flood, Nepal (2026)
description:
On 26 August 2026, an outburst flood swept the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river corridor across the Nepal–China border, killing at least 160 people and leaving hundreds missing, including tourists and workers. Nepal Police reported at least 157 deaths, while Chinese state media reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Gyirong County, Tibet Autonomous Region. Preliminary expert assessment attributes the trigger to an ice and rock avalanche from a glacier in the upper catchment; the cause remains under investigation, and all casualty figures are provisional as of 26 August 2026 and were still rising at time of release.

Update, 12 October 2026: early on 11 October 2026 a second very large mass movement struck the Budhi Gandaki valley in Gorkha district, less than 100 km west of the Rasuwa event. A rock (possibly rock-ice) avalanche from the southern slopes of the Chamar massif appears to have dammed the Syar river; the subsequent breach sent a debris flood down the Budhi Gandaki, affecting several settlements. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) issued a warning and evacuated residents. The source area and volume were still being determined at time of release. Collections for this event cover the Chamar slopes, the Syar confluence and the Budhi Gandaki downstream to Arughat, with PlanetScope imagery from the day before (10 October) and the two days after (11-12 October).
